items.title: 川普宣布：即刻起俄烏雙方同意「能源停火」！
items.title_en: Trump Announces: Effective Immediately, Russia and Ukraine Agree to an “Energy Ceasefire”
paras: 美國總統川普11日（周日）在社交媒體發文，稱即刻起俄烏衝突進入「能源停火」狀態。
英國國防大臣韋斯·斯特里廷11日說，英國不支持美俄兩國領袖就俄羅斯向美國及全球市場提供柴油達成一致。
斯特里廷在《BBC》當天播出的節目中說，川普此舉很大程度上是因為他面臨期中選舉，迫於緩解民眾生活成本壓力而同俄方就柴油供應達成一致。
《BBC》指出，自美國和以色列對伊朗發動軍事打擊以來，美國燃油價格高漲，俄羅斯向美國提供柴油，目的是降低美國國內燃油價格。
美國財政部外國資產控制辦公室9日發布公告，稱在未來幾個月放鬆針對俄羅斯柴油貿易的制裁，以緩解美國內柴油供應緊張，平抑油價。
川普同日宣布，美俄元首就俄羅斯向美國及全球市場提供柴油達成一致。
烏克蘭總統澤倫斯基隨後表示，美方允許俄羅斯出售石油產品「就是在投資戰爭」，他很失望，感覺「被背叛」。
paras_en: U.S. President Donald Trump posted on social media on Sunday the 11th, saying that the Russia‑Ukraine conflict has entered an “energy ceasefire” as of now.

British Defence Secretary Wes Streeting said on the 11th that the United Kingdom does not support an agreement between the U.S. and Russian leaders on Russia supplying diesel to the United States and global markets.

Streeting told a BBC programme that Trump’s move is largely driven by his upcoming midterm elections and the pressure to ease the public’s cost‑of‑living concerns, leading him to reach a diesel‑supply deal with Russia.

The BBC noted that since the United States and Israel launched military strikes against Iran, U.S. fuel prices have surged, and Russia’s provision of diesel to the United States is intended to lower domestic fuel costs.

The U.S. Treasury’s Office of Foreign Assets Control issued a notice on the 9th that it will relax sanctions on Russian diesel trade over the coming months to ease domestic diesel shortages and stabilize oil prices.
Trump also announced on the same day that the heads of state of the United States and Russia have reached an agreement on Russia supplying diesel to the United States and global markets.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky later said that the U.S. allowing Russia to sell petroleum products is “investing in the war,” expressing disappointment and feeling “betrayed.”

items.title: 歐洲最大晶圓廠布局物理AI！格羅方德砸11億歐元擴建德國晶圓廠、2028年啟動生產
items.title_en: Europe’s Largest Wafer Plant Expands into Physical AI! GlobalFoundries Invests €1.1 Billion to Expand German Wafer Plant, Production Starts 2028
paras: 全球晶圓代工大廠格羅方德(GFS-US) 加碼布局物理人工智慧（Physical AI）市場。格羅方德近日宣布，位於德國德勒斯登的SPRINT晶圓廠擴建計畫正式封頂，總投資金額達11億歐元，並同步推出新一代全耗盡型絕緣層上覆矽（FD-SOI）技術平台FDX Fusion，瞄準機器人、智慧汽車與工業自動化等應用。
隨著AI應用從雲端資料中心延伸至實體設備，半導體產業對晶片的需求也逐漸從追求運算效能，擴大至低功耗、即時反應、感測整合與高可靠性。
格羅方德希望藉由FDX Fusion平台，切入實體AI帶動的新一波晶片需求，並透過德國擴產計畫強化歐洲製造布局。

德勒斯登廠投資11億歐元　2028年底年產能逾百萬片

格羅方德此次透過SPRINT計畫擴建德國德勒斯登廠的300毫米晶圓製造能力，預計2028年底完成後，年產能將超過100萬片，屆時可望成為歐洲最大的晶圓代工基地。
目前德勒斯登廠約有3,000名員工，設有約6萬平方公尺的無塵室與實驗室，300毫米晶圓年產能約95萬片。格羅方德自2009年以來，已在當地累計投資超過100億歐元。
格羅方德表示，新增產能將主要服務汽車、航太、工業物聯網及國防等領域。這些應用對半導體供應穩定性、資訊安全及長期運作可靠性均有較高要求。
SPRINT計畫獲得歐盟、德國聯邦政府及薩克森邦政府支持，並納入《歐洲晶片法案》相關架構。
格羅方德指出，擴產也將協助公司為關鍵基礎設施及航太客戶提供限於歐洲境內使用的製程與資料流程。

FDX Fusion鎖定物理AI　整合運算、感測與連接能力

除了擴充產能，格羅方德也在封頂儀式上發表新一代FD-SOI平台FDX Fusion，目標是滿足物理AI對半導體的特殊需求。
物理AI是指將人工智慧導入實體環境，使機器人、汽車及工業設備能夠感知周遭環境、進行判斷並採取行動。相較於主要部署在資料中心的AI運算，這類應用更重視即時處理能力、能源效率，以及在複雜環境下持續穩定運作的能力。
格羅方德以STAC工作負載概括相關需求，涵蓋感知（Sense）、思考（Think）、行動（Act）、再次思考（Think）及溝通（Communicate）等環節。
FDX Fusion的設計方向，是將AI處理、感測、控制及連接能力整合至同一技術平台，讓晶片能因應邊緣AI設備在運算與能源消耗之間的平衡需求。

晶片密度提升逾兩倍　首代技術達7奈米級數位效能

在技術規格方面，格羅方德表示，第一代FDX Fusion預計可提供相當於7奈米級的數位效能，晶片密度則預計較第一代FDX技術提高逾兩倍。
新平台結合基板工程、前段電晶體技術、後段互連及系統整合能力，並支援類比與混合訊號、高效能射頻、嵌入式非揮發性記憶體、低漏電運作及記憶體內運算等功能。
格羅方德也指出，FDX Fusion的射頻性能最高可達0.5 THz ft/fmax，期望藉此滿足邊緣AI設備整合運算、通訊與控制功能的需求。
格羅方德CMOS業務資深副總裁Ed Kaste表示，隨著智慧技術從雲端延伸至能夠即時處理資料、並與實體環境互動的系統，物理AI正帶動新一類半導體需求。FDX Fusion則透過基板、電晶體及互連結構的技術創新，進一步拓展格羅方德的FD-SOI技術路線。
相較於資料中心AI晶片著重大規模平行運算，機器人、智慧汽車及工業設備通常需要在有限功耗下，持續處理感測器資料並快速做出反應。格羅方德希望利用FD-SOI技術的特性，進一步拓展在低功耗、高可靠性及射頻整合方面的應用。

英飛凌、博世、恩智浦力挺　強化歐洲半導體生態系

FDX Fusion的發布也獲得多家半導體與工業企業支持。
英飛凌外部晶圓製造執行副總裁Patrick Pötsch表示，英飛凌正與格羅方德加強合作，共同定義及探索用於下一代雷達與無線通訊產品的7奈米級FDX Fusion技術。
博世移動電子積體電路業務部資深副總裁Axel Kaschner指出，格羅方德的FDX技術路線圖有助於推動整合感測、控制、連接及高效率邊緣智慧的半導體平台，支援下一代機器人與自動化系統。
歐洲微電子研究機構CEA-Leti執行長Sébastien Dauvé則表示，該機構透過FAMES試產線，持續推進歐洲FD-SOI技術發展，並促進相關技術在不同應用領域的普及。
恩智浦半導體(NXPI-US) 執行副總裁暨技術長Lars Reger認為，物理AI正在改變機器與實體世界互動的方式，也使邊緣端對安全、可靠及低延遲運算提出更高要求。
西門子數位工業總裁Cedrik Neike也表示，半導體是機器人、互聯設備及將AI導入實體世界與工業領域的重要基礎。
此外，特斯拉(TSLA-US) 供應鏈副總裁Karn Budhiraj指出，開發及製造用於邊緣處理的高效能運算設備，是推動下一代先進機器人與自主系統發展的重要環節。

2027年交付展示晶片　2028年啟動生產

在商業化時程方面，格羅方德預計2027年初向早期客戶交付FDX Fusion展示晶片，並於2027年年中推出初版製程設計套件（PDK），讓客戶展開設計與開發工作。
格羅方德規劃於2028年在德勒斯登廠啟動FDX Fusion晶片生產，目前已與多家客戶進行早期開發及評估。公司表示，平台將採用經最佳化的製程流程與成本結構，以利客戶加速原型開發及產品上市。
隨著AI逐步進入機器人、智慧汽車、工業自動化及自主系統，半導體市場的競爭重點也正逐漸擴大。除了運算效能，功耗、即時反應、感測與通訊整合，以及長期運作的可靠性，都將影響晶片在實體AI領域的應用。
相較於聚焦先進製程與高效能運算的晶圓代工競爭，格羅方德選擇透過FD-SOI技術深化差異化布局，並結合德國擴產計畫，爭取汽車、工業及其他對供應穩定性有較高要求的市場。
FDX Fusion能否順利推進量產、獲得更多客戶採用，仍有待後續發展，但格羅方德已將物理AI列為新一代技術平台的重要應用方向。
paras_en: GlobalFoundries (GFS‑US), a leading semiconductor foundry, is ramping up its presence in the Physical AI market. The company recently announced that the SPRINT wafer plant in Dresden, Germany, has officially reached its investment cap, with a total investment of €1.1 billion. At the same time, it unveiled the next‑generation fully‑depleted silicon on insulator (FD‑SOI) technology platform, FDX Fusion, targeting applications in robotics, smart vehicles, and industrial automation.

As AI moves from cloud data centers to physical devices, the semiconductor industry’s demand for chips is shifting from pure compute performance to low power, real‑time response, integrated sensing, and high reliability.
GlobalFoundries aims to tap the new wave of chip demand driven by Physical AI through the FDX Fusion platform, and to strengthen its European manufacturing footprint via the German expansion plan.

The Dresden plant’s €1.1 billion investment will expand its 300‑mm wafer manufacturing capacity. By the end of 2028, the annual output is expected to exceed one million wafers, potentially making it Europe’s largest foundry base.

The Dresden facility currently employs about 3,000 people, houses roughly 60,000 m² of cleanroom and laboratory space, and has a 300‑mm wafer annual capacity of about 950,000. Since 2009, GlobalFoundries has invested over €10 billion in the region.

The added capacity will primarily serve automotive, aerospace, industrial IoT, and defense sectors, all of which demand high supply stability, information security, and long‑term operational reliability.
The SPRINT plan has received support from the EU, the German federal government, and the Saxony state government, and is incorporated into the European Chips Act framework.
GlobalFoundries notes that the expansion will also help the company provide processes and data flows limited to use within Europe for critical infrastructure and aerospace customers.
FDX Fusion targets Physical AI, integrating compute, sensing, and connectivity capabilities.

Physical AI refers to embedding AI into the physical environment, enabling robots, vehicles, and industrial equipment to perceive surroundings, make decisions, and act. Compared to data‑center AI, these applications prioritize real‑time processing, energy efficiency, and continuous stable operation in complex environments.
GlobalFoundries summarizes the related needs with the STAC workload, covering Sense, Think, Act, Think again, and Communicate stages.

FDX Fusion’s design goal is to integrate AI processing, sensing, control, and connectivity onto a single technology platform, allowing chips to balance compute and energy consumption for edge AI devices.

In terms of technical specifications, GlobalFoundries says the first‑generation FDX Fusion will deliver digital performance equivalent to 7 nm, with chip density more than twice that of the first‑generation FDX technology.

The new platform combines substrate engineering, front‑end transistor technology, back‑end interconnect, and system integration, supporting analog and mixed‑signal, high‑performance RF, embedded non‑volatile memory, low‑leakage operation, and in‑memory computing functions.
GlobalFoundries also notes that FDX Fusion’s RF performance can reach up to 0.5 THz ft/fmax, aiming to meet edge AI devices’ needs for integrated compute, communication, and control.

Ed Kaste, Senior VP of GlobalFoundries’ CMOS business, says that as smart technologies move from the cloud to systems that can process data in real time and interact with the physical environment, Physical AI is driving a new class of semiconductor demand. FDX Fusion expands GlobalFoundries’ FD‑SOI roadmap through innovations in substrate, transistor, and interconnect structures.

Unlike data‑center AI chips that focus on large‑scale parallel compute, robots, smart cars, and industrial equipment typically need to continuously process sensor data and react quickly under limited power. GlobalFoundries hopes to leverage FD‑SOI’s characteristics to further expand applications in low power, high reliability, and RF integration.
The launch of FDX Fusion also received support from several semiconductor and industrial companies.

Patrick Pötsch, Vice President of External Wafer Fabrication at Infineon, says Infineon is strengthening its partnership with GlobalFoundries to jointly define and explore 7 nm‑level FDX Fusion technology for next‑generation radar and wireless communication products.

Axel Kaschner, Senior VP of Bosch Mobile Electronics IC Business, points out that GlobalFoundries’ FDX technology roadmap helps drive integrated sensing, control, connectivity, and high‑efficiency edge intelligence semiconductor platforms, supporting next‑generation robots and automation systems.

Sébastien Dauvé, CEO of the European Microelectronics Research Institute CEA‑Leti, says the institute’s FAMES pilot line continues to advance European FD‑SOI technology development and promotes its adoption across various application domains.

Lars Reger, Executive VP and CTO of NXP Semiconductors (NXPI‑US), believes Physical AI is changing how machines interact with the physical world, and is raising higher demands for security, reliability, and low‑latency compute at the edge.

Cedrik Neike, President of Siemens Digital Industries, also states that semiconductors are a critical foundation for robots, connected devices, and bringing AI into the physical world and industrial sectors.

Additionally, Tesla’s supply‑chain VP Karn Budhiraj notes that developing and manufacturing high‑performance compute devices for edge processing is a key enabler for next‑generation advanced robots and autonomous systems.

In terms of commercialization timelines, GlobalFoundries plans to deliver FDX Fusion demonstration chips to early customers in early 2027, and to launch a first‑edition process design kit (PDK) in mid‑2027, enabling customers to begin design and development work.

GlobalFoundries plans to start FDX Fusion chip production at the Dresden plant in 2028, and has already engaged in early development and evaluation with several customers. The company says the platform will use an optimized process flow and cost structure to accelerate prototype development and product launch for customers.

As AI gradually enters robotics, smart vehicles, industrial automation, and autonomous systems, the semiconductor market’s competitive focus is also expanding. Beyond compute performance, power consumption, real‑time response, integrated sensing and communication, and long‑term reliability will influence chip applications in Physical AI.

Compared to the focus on advanced process nodes and high‑performance compute in foundry competition, GlobalFoundries chooses to deepen differentiation through FD‑SOI technology and combine it with the German expansion plan to target automotive, industrial, and other markets that demand higher supply stability.

Whether FDX Fusion can successfully advance to mass production and gain wider customer adoption remains to be seen, but GlobalFoundries has already positioned Physical AI as a key application direction for its next‑generation technology platform.

items.title: 本週操盤筆記：美CPI牽動升息預期！美股財報季開跑、台積電法說和ASML接力登場
items.title_en: This Week's Trading Notes: US CPI Drives Rate Hike Expectations! US Earnings Season Kicks Off, TSMC and ASML Appear in Successive Briefings
paras: 本週國際大事包括美國9月消費者物價指數(CPI)，這是聯準會(Fed)10月底決策會議登場前最後一批重要經濟數據之一。大型銀行將為財報季揭開序幕，台積電和艾司摩爾的營運和財測，將是投資人觀察人工智慧(AI)投資是否繼續推升半導體設備和晶圓代工需求的指標。

1、美國CPI牽動升息預期

美國將在週三(14日)公布9月CPI，路透訪調的分析師預估9月CPI年增率將達3.7%，排除波動較大的能源與食品價格後，核心CPI年增率預估為2.5%，漲幅相對溫和。Fed的年度通膨目標為2%。
在美國公布8月核心CPI以四個月來最快速度上升之後，Fed在9月宣布三年來首度升息。目前市場對10月再次升息的押注已有所降溫，但如果9月CPI高於預期，可能再度改變市場看法。
分析師指出，若核心服務通膨有所降溫，才能讓人更有把握認為，Fed不必像市場目前預期的那樣採取激進措施。
接著，週四公布的生產者物價指數(PPI)將進一步補足通膨情勢的全貌，當天也將發布零售銷售數據。

2、銀行股揭開財報季序幕 債券殖利率上升壓力罩頂

美國第3季財報季由大型銀行股率先登場，投資人將關注高利率如何影響資本市場與消費支出。每季財報季通常由銀行股揭開序幕，其業績也能反映美國整體經濟的健康狀況。
華爾街六大銀行中，有四家將於週二公布財報，分別是摩根大通(JPMorgan Chase)(JPM-US)、高盛(Goldman Sachs)(GS-US)、花旗集團(Citigroup)(C-US)及富國銀行(Wells Fargo)(WFC-US)。摩根士丹利(Morgan Stanley)(MS-US)與美國銀行(Bank of America)(BAC-US)則將於週三公布業績。
市場預期企業獲利年增幅最高可達20%，然而，美國公債殖利率攀升至數十年高點，已對銀行股造成壓力。KBW銀行指數目前較8月高點下跌約13%。

3、台積電、ASML考驗AI行情

科技領域方面，晶圓代工龍頭台積電(TSM-US)(2330-TW)、半導體設備商艾司摩爾(ASML-US)本週也將公布財報。
台積電週四(15日)的法說會可能是半導體類股本週最重要的一天，若交出強勁的財報和財測，可能出現規模驚人的漲勢。
科技媒體《Wccftech》報導，市場聚焦台積電A14製程的進度、資本支出如反映公司對未來人工智慧(AI)需求看法、CoWoS先進封裝技術，以及明年漲價的可能性。此外，投資人也關注是否會進一步說明與馬斯克旗下Terafab晶片製造計畫潛在合作案的細節。
至於艾司摩爾，分析師指出，如果上修財測，並釋出強勁的需求訊號，市場對AI熱潮仍在推動晶圓廠投資將更有信心。這也可能有利於其他半導體設備股，例如科林研發(Lam Research)(LRCX-US)和應用材料(Applied Materials)(AMAT-US)。

4、公債殖利率持續攀升 市場仍面臨重大風險

債券拋售潮至今仍看不出明顯緩和跡象，美國與法國公債殖利率已升至24年來新高，市場波動也處於高檔。
法國與德國10年期公債殖利率利差目前約為136個基點，一個月前還不到100個基點。法國風險溢價在短時間內大幅攀升，也對義大利同類資產、歐元及歐洲股市造成壓力。
市場近期也開始將矛頭指向避險基金的角色。這類追求短期收益的資金，近來在攸關金融體系穩定的重要債券市場中，參與程度持續提高。

5、IMF亞洲年會登場 全球成長、債務與地緣政治成焦點

國際貨幣基金(IMF)預定週二公布最新《世界經濟展望》。伊朗戰爭已迫使IMF今年兩度下修全球國內生產毛額(GDP)成長預測，而IMF總裁喬治艾娃(Kristalina Georgieva)已經暗示，最新展望恐怕不會令人樂觀，壓力來自能源價格高漲、公共債務創新高，以及債券市場情緒緊繃。
中東與烏克蘭衝突等地緣政治分歧，預料將成為年會上的重要議題。此外，美中兩國在人工智慧(AI)領域展開競爭，如何監管AI同樣備受關注。與會官員也密切關注，法國是否會讓歐元區再度面臨債務壓力。
paras_en: This week’s major international events include the US September Consumer Price Index (CPI), one of the last important economic data points before the Federal Reserve’s late‑October policy meeting. Large banks will open the earnings season, and the operating results and forecasts of TSMC and ASML will be key indicators for investors watching whether AI‑driven investment continues to boost demand for semiconductor equipment and wafer‑foundry services.
This week’s trading notes (20261012–1018)

1. US CPI Drives Rate‑Hike Expectations
The United States will release the September CPI on Wednesday (the 14th). Reuters‑surveyed analysts forecast a year‑over‑year CPI increase of 3.7%. Excluding the more volatile energy and food components, core CPI is expected to rise 2.5% year‑over‑year, a relatively modest gain. The Fed’s annual inflation target is 2%.

After the US reported August core CPI rising at the fastest pace in four months, the Fed announced its first rate hike in three years in September. Market bets on another October hike have eased, but a CPI reading above expectations could again shift market sentiment.
Analysts note that only if core services inflation cools can investors feel more confident that the Fed will not need to take the aggressive actions the market currently anticipates.
Next, Thursday’s Producer Price Index (PPI) will further fill in the picture of inflation, and retail sales data will also be released that day.

2. Bank Stocks Open the Earnings Season, Rising Bond Yields Put Pressure on the Top
The US third‑quarter earnings season will start with large‑cap bank stocks, and investors will watch how higher rates affect capital markets and consumer spending. Each earnings season typically begins with banks, whose results also reflect the overall health of the US economy.

Among Wall Street’s six biggest banks, four will report on Tuesday: JPMorgan Chase (JPM‑US), Goldman Sachs (GS‑US), Citigroup (C‑US) and Wells Fargo (WFC‑US). Morgan Stanley (MS‑US) and Bank of America (BAC‑US) will release results on Wednesday.

The market expects corporate earnings growth of up to 20% year‑over‑year, but US Treasury yields have climbed to multi‑decade highs, already weighing on bank stocks. The KBW Bank Index is down about 13% from its August peak.

3. TSMC and ASML Test the AI Rally
In the technology sector, wafer‑fab leader TSMC (TSM‑US, 2330‑TW) and semiconductor‑equipment maker ASML (ASML‑US) will also report earnings this week.
TSMC’s briefing on Thursday (the 15th) could be the most important day for semiconductor stocks this week; a strong earnings report and outlook could trigger a spectacular price surge.

Tech media outlet Wccftech reported that the market is focusing on TSMC’s A14 process progress, capital expenditures as a gauge of the company’s view on future AI demand, CoWoS advanced packaging technology, and the possibility of a price increase next year. Investors are also watching for any further details on a potential collaboration with Elon Musk’s Terafab chip‑manufacturing plan.

As for ASML, analysts say that an upgraded forecast and a strong demand signal would reinforce market confidence that the AI boom continues to drive wafer‑fab investment. This could also benefit other semiconductor‑equipment stocks such as Lam Research (LRCX‑US) and Applied Materials (AMAT‑US).

4. Treasury Yields Keep Climbing, Market Still Faces Major Risks
Bond sell‑offs show no clear signs of easing; US and French sovereign yields have risen to 24‑year highs, keeping market volatility elevated.

The spread between French and German 10‑year yields is now about 136 basis points, up from under 100 basis points a month ago. France’s risk premium has surged in a short period, pressuring Italian assets, the euro and European equities.

Markets have also begun to point the finger at the role of hedge funds. These short‑term‑return‑seeking funds have recently increased their participation in the bond markets that are critical to financial‑system stability.

5. IMF Asia Meeting Kicks Off, Global Growth, Debt and Geopolitics in Focus
The International Monetary Fund (IMF) is set to release its latest World Economic Outlook on Tuesday. The Iran war has forced the IMF to cut global GDP growth forecasts twice this year, and IMF Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva has hinted that the new outlook is unlikely to be optimistic, with pressure coming from high energy prices, record‑high public debt and strained bond‑market sentiment.

Geopolitical tensions such as the Middle‑East and Ukraine conflicts are expected to be major topics at the meeting. In addition, US‑China competition in AI and how to regulate the technology are also under close watch. Officials will also be closely monitoring whether France could cause the euro‑area to face renewed debt pressures.

items.title: 逾1400億美元交易+近千億股權投資！專家：輝達成「AI央行」　用資本綁定對沖客戶集中風險
items.title_en: Over $140 Billion in Deals + Nearly $100 Billion in Equity Investments! Experts Say Nvidia Becomes an “AI Central Bank,” Using Capital to Hedge Concentrated Customer Risk
paras: 外媒最新報導指出，輝達過去數月完成超過1400億美元交易，截至7月底股權投資市值接近1000億美元，另有約250億美元未來出資承諾，下一步投資重心轉向人形機器人、自動駕駛與端側AI模型。
多位與輝達合作的交行、律師及創投人士向科技媒體《The Information》報導，這輪佈局目的不只是賣GPU，而是用股權、授權、人才引進把模型與應用場景綁進輝達算力圈，而驅動力來自客戶過度集中，在7月為止的2027財年上半年，輝達前三大客戶分別貢獻16%、15%、13%收入，合計44%，2026財年僅前兩家合計36%，2023財年無單一客戶超10%。
同期，前五家應收帳款佔比升至70%，高於1月的56%。大客戶既買晶片也自研ASIC，使黃仁勳有動機把收入來源從「少數超大資料中心」擴到「數千模型、數千場景」。
報導指出，開源與模型層最重一筆是Hugging Face，其創辦人Clem Delangue今夏主動聯絡黃仁勳；OpenAI曾因系統安全事件後洽談1億美元投資，Salesforce亦有收購意，最終輝達以129億美元收購，對其約1.5億美元年化收入相當於80餘倍市銷率。
輝達另以60億美元與Poolside達成軟體授權及人才交易，推進自研Nemotron；據悉洽談投資Mira Murati創辦的Thinking Machines約25億美元，並已布局Anthropic、xAI、Reflection AI等。
端側與Agent是下一戰場。Perplexity工程師6月用兩台DGX Spark演示本地多步Agent，黃仁勳主導後續談判。據悉，Srinivas曾提全資收購，雙方轉向技術授權與出資，8月底合作發Portable Computer，輝達擬以約30億美元參與Perplexity新輪融資、前估值約350億美元。
人形機器人方面，據稱與Figure洽談追加投資約10億美元；自駕與邊緣推理亦列入優先項，配合DGX Spark、Jetson等把推理從雲端外溢到機器與終端。
但資料中心信用部位已引發擔憂。在軟銀SB Energy俄亥俄聯邦用地項目中，輝達起初討論對OpenAI租約提供最高2500億美元信用支持，後壓至首階段1050億美元；黃仁勳8月頻問CDS利差，市場顯示違約互換一度走闊。
輝達另外還參與OpenAI新輪300億美元、最後100億美元10月1日交割，8月召集黑石、Apollo、高盛等六家機構為5000億美元硬體融資組盤，輝達對部分交易最高支撐25%。
交易執行由甲骨文前高管Vishal Bhagwati統籌企發，黃仁勳親抓定價；OpenRouter曾因評估太慢而被Stripe約80億美元截胡，其後兩個月加速簽單。
對投資人而言，輝達正從「晶片供應商」變成「生態出資人」，好處是綁住需求、攤薄客戶自研風險，代價是應收、擔保、股權與CDS同步上升。
上月，黃仁勳在高盛舊金山科技大會稱「我是知情投資者、不承擔無確定性風險」，但市場更關心的是，當AI資本開支週期回檔，千億級承諾會否由股價與利差同時計價。
paras_en: Foreign media reports that Nvidia completed more than $140 billion in transactions over the past few months, and by the end of July its equity‑investment market value was close to $100 billion, with about $25 billion in future funding commitments. The next investment focus shifts to humanoid robots, autonomous driving and edge‑side AI models.

Several banks, lawyers and venture‑capitalists who work with Nvidia told tech outlet The Information that this round of positioning is not just about selling GPUs; it ties models and use‑cases into Nvidia’s compute ecosystem through equity, licensing and talent recruitment. The driver is customer concentration: in the first half of fiscal 2027 (through July) Nvidia’s top three customers contributed 16%, 15% and 13% of revenue respectively – a combined 44%; in fiscal 2026 the top two accounted for 36%; and in fiscal 2023 no single customer exceeded 10%.

At the same time, the share of the top five accounts receivable rose to 70%, up from 56% in January. Large customers both buy chips and develop their own ASICs, giving CEO Jensen Huang incentive to expand revenue sources from “a few massive data centers” to “thousands of models, thousands of scenarios.”

The report notes that the biggest deal on the open‑source and model layer was with Hugging Face, whose founder Clem Delangue reached out to Jensen Huang this summer; OpenAI, after a system‑security incident, discussed a $100 million investment; Salesforce also showed acquisition interest, but Nvidia ultimately acquired it for $12.9 billion, a valuation roughly 80‑times its annualized revenue of about $150 million.

Nvidia also struck a $6 billion software‑licensing and talent‑deal with Poolside to advance its in‑house Nemotron. It is reported to be negotiating a roughly $2.5 billion investment in Thinking Machines, founded by Mira Murati, and has already placed bets on Anthropic, xAI and Reflection AI among others.

Edge‑side and Agent AI are the next battlegrounds. In June, Perplexity engineers demonstrated a local multi‑step Agent using two DGX Spark systems, with Jensen Huang leading the follow‑up negotiations. Sources say Srinivas once proposed a full‑cash acquisition, but the parties shifted to technology licensing and equity investment, co‑developing a Portable Computer by the end of August. Nvidia plans to put about $3 billion into Perplexity’s new financing round, which values the company at roughly $35 billion.

On the humanoid‑robot front, Nvidia is said to be negotiating an additional roughly $1 billion investment with Figure; autonomous‑driving and edge inference are also priority areas, leveraging DGX Spark, Jetson and other hardware to push inference from the cloud onto machines and endpoints.

However, the data‑center credit exposure has raised concerns. In SoftBank’s SB Energy Ohio federal‑land project, Nvidia initially discussed providing up to $250 billion of credit support for OpenAI lease agreements, later scaling back to an initial $105 billion tranche; Jensen Huang repeatedly asked about CDS spreads in August, and the market showed widening credit‑default swap spreads.

Nvidia also participated in OpenAI’s new $30 billion round and a final $10 billion tranche closing on October 1. In August it convened Blackstone, Apollo, Goldman Sachs and four other firms to arrange a $500 billion hardware‑financing package, with Nvidia offering up to 25% support on certain deals.

Deal execution was coordinated by former Oracle executive Vishal Bhagwati, with Jensen Huang directly handling pricing. OpenRouter, after being deemed too slow in evaluation, was snapped up by Stripe for about $8 billion, and accelerated contract signing followed two months later.

For investors, Nvidia is transitioning from a “chip supplier” to an “ecosystem investor.” The benefit is locking in demand and diluting customers’ in‑house development risk; the cost is rising accounts receivable, guarantees, equity stakes and CDS exposure.

Last month, Jensen Huang told Goldman Sachs’ San Francisco tech conference, “I am an informed investor and do not assume undefined risk,” but the market is more focused on whether, when the AI‑capex cycle pulls back, the multi‑hundred‑billion commitments will be priced jointly by stock price and credit spreads.

items.title: 黃仁勳、蘇姿丰、馬斯克獲美國國家科學獎章  輝達、AMD、特斯拉科技實力受肯定
items.title_en: Jensen Huang, Lisa Su, and Elon Musk Receive U.S. National Science Medals; Nvidia, AMD, and Tesla’s Technological Strength Recognized
paras: 美國總統川普於當地時間8日舉行「科學：新黃金時代」（Science: A New Golden Age）高峰會，並向6名科技業領袖頒發國家科學獎章及國家技術與創新獎章。其中，輝達(NVDA-US) 執行長黃仁勳、超微半導體(AMD-US) 執行長蘇姿丰及特斯拉(TSLA-US) 執行長馬斯克獲頒國家科學獎章，肯定他們在半導體、人工智慧（AI）及太空科技等領域的貢獻。
根據白宮聲明，美國國家科學獎章自1963年起頒發，旨在表彰對美國科學發展有傑出貢獻的人士；國家技術與創新獎章則於1985年設立，表揚透過技術創新促進美國經濟發展、改善生活品質的傑出人才。
在半導體與AI領域，黃仁勳獲獎的主要原因，是他推動圖形處理器（GPU）從傳統圖形運算工具，發展為可執行通用運算的架構。
白宮指出，黃仁勳透過處理器設計與軟體技術創新，促進大規模平行運算發展，為科學運算及超級智慧（Superintelligence）領域的重大突破奠定基礎。
蘇姿丰則因長期投入半導體工程與高效能運算（HPC）技術獲得肯定。白宮特別指出，她在處理器架構及小晶片（Chiplet）整合技術上的創新，協助推動全球首部百億億次級超級電腦問世，進一步突破高效能運算的技術限制。
馬斯克獲獎則與其在太空探索、智慧系統、通訊及製造技術等領域的工程成就有關。白宮認為，相關技術突破不僅拓展太空探索與通訊技術的發展，也有助於提升美國的科技領導地位及製造業競爭力。
除上述3人外，Google(GOOGL-US) 共同創辦人布林（Sergey Brin）也獲頒國家科學獎章，表彰他在資訊檢索及資料處理演算法方面的貢獻。
另外，戴爾科技(DELL-US) 創辦人戴爾（Michael Dell）與微軟(MSFT-US) 執行長納德拉（Satya Nadella）則獲頒國家技術與創新獎章，分別因推動個人與企業運算普及，以及雲端運算和超大規模AI基礎設施發展而獲得肯定。
白宮科學與技術政策辦公室主任克拉齊奧斯（Michael Kratsios）表示，6名獲獎者在各自領域帶來重大變革，並為現今廣泛使用的技術奠定基礎。
他指出，政府持續推動科學研究與技術創新政策固然重要，但真正促成科學突破的關鍵，仍在於創新人才的洞察力與創造力。
paras_en: U.S. President Donald Trump held a "Science: A New Golden Age" summit on the 8th local time and presented the National Science Medal and the National Medal of Technology and Innovation to six technology leaders. Nvidia (NVDA-US) CEO Jensen Huang, AMD (AMD-US) CEO Lisa Su, and Tesla (TSLA-US) CEO Elon Musk were awarded the National Science Medal in recognition of their contributions to semiconductors, artificial intelligence (AI) and space technology.

According to a White House statement, the National Science Medal has been awarded since 1963 to honor individuals who have made outstanding contributions to the development of science in the United States; the National Medal of Technology and Innovation was established in 1985 to recognize outstanding talent whose technological innovations promote economic growth and improve quality of life.

In the semiconductor and AI fields, the main reason Huang received the award was his role in transforming graphics processing units (GPUs) from traditional graphics tools into architectures capable of general‑purpose computing.

The White House noted that Huang’s innovations in processor design and software have advanced large‑scale parallel computing, laying the groundwork for major breakthroughs in scientific computing and super‑intelligence.

Lisa Su was recognized for her long‑term commitment to semiconductor engineering and high‑performance computing (HPC). The statement highlighted her innovations in processor architecture and chiplet integration, which helped bring the world’s first exaflop‑class supercomputer to market and pushed the limits of HPC technology.

Musk’s award was tied to his engineering achievements in space exploration, intelligent systems, communications and manufacturing technologies. The White House said these breakthroughs not only expand space and communications capabilities but also bolster U.S. technological leadership and manufacturing competitiveness.
In addition to the three above, Google (GOOGL-US) co‑founder Sergey Brin also received the National Science Medal for his contributions to information retrieval and data‑processing algorithms.

Dell Technologies (DELL-US) founder Michael Dell and Microsoft (MSFT-US) CEO Satya Nadella were each awarded the National Medal of Technology and Innovation, recognized respectively for driving the widespread adoption of personal and enterprise computing and for advancing cloud computing and massive‑scale AI infrastructure.

Michael Kratsios, director of the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy, said the six honorees have brought transformative change to their fields and laid the foundation for the technologies widely used today.

He added that while continued government support for scientific research and innovation policy is important, the key to real scientific breakthroughs remains the insight and creativity of innovative talent.

items.title: 日本企業破產創13年同期新高！升息、缺工與成本上漲夾擊　25.1萬家殭屍企業面臨危機
items.title_en: Japanese Corporate Bankruptcies Reach 13‑Year High in Same Period! Rising Rates, Labor Shortages, and Cost Increases Strike
paras: 日本貨幣政策逐步緊縮，企業經營壓力也持續升高。東京商工調查公司近日公布的數據顯示，2026會計年度上半年（4月至9月），日本負債額達1,000萬日元以上的企業破產案件共5,373件，年增3.8%，創13年同期新高；破產負債總額達8,561.69億日元，年增23.5%。
從企業規模來看，負債未滿1億日元的企業占整體破產案件77%，員工人數未滿10人的企業更占90.6%。
此外，日本傳統企業也難以倖免，今年1月至8月，已有112家創立逾百年的企業進入法律破產程序。
分析指出，這波企業倒閉潮背後，不只是升息帶來的融資成本增加，還包括原物料與薪資上漲、勞動力短缺，以及長期仰賴低利率維持營運的企業面臨債務壓力。
隨著日本銀行（日本央行）持續推進貨幣政策正常化，企業的財務脆弱性正逐漸浮現。

日本企業面臨三重壓力　升息加劇中小企業資金困境

日本企業破產案件持續增加，主要受到三大因素影響，其中升息推高資金成本，是企業經營壓力加重的重要原因。
企業從採購原物料、支付薪資到完成訂單並收取貨款，往往存在一定的資金週轉時間。當自有資金不足時，企業必須仰賴銀行貸款支應營運需求，因此借款利率上升，便會直接增加企業的資金成本。
更重要的是，原物料與薪資同步上漲，使企業必須準備更多週轉資金。如果產品銷售放緩、客戶延遲付款，企業不僅要承擔更高的利息支出，資金遭占用的時間也會拉長，進一步增加財務負擔。
當企業獲利能力下滑、償債能力轉弱，銀行也可能重新評估放款風險，使企業取得新貸款的成本進一步提高，形成經營壓力與融資困難相互加劇的局面。
東京商工調查數據顯示，2026會計年度上半年，日本因物價上漲而破產的企業達436家，年增17.8%；其中，資本額未滿1,000萬日元的企業占63.9%，反映資本規模較小的業者更容易受到成本上漲衝擊。
另一項關鍵因素，是企業將成本轉嫁給客戶的能力有限。帝國資料銀行（Teikoku Databank）今年7月針對10,518家企業進行調查，結果顯示，日本企業整體成本轉嫁率僅39.9%，餐飲業更只有28.7%；能夠完全轉嫁新增成本的企業占比僅3.4%。

高齡化加劇缺工危機　人工成本上漲成破產主因之一

除了融資成本增加，日本企業還必須面對勞動力短缺與薪資上漲的雙重挑戰。
日本總務省9月公布的數據顯示，65歲以上人口占總人口比率達29.6%，創歷史新高。帝國資料銀行今年7月的調查也指出，51.3%的受訪企業表示正式員工人數不足，顯示缺工問題仍然普遍。
對企業而言，缺工不僅可能限制生產與接單能力，也迫使業者提高薪資，以吸引及留住員工。
日本各地自2026年10月起陸續調整最低工資，全國加權平均時薪將達1,177日元，較前一年增加56日元，漲幅約5%。
企業若要消化增加的人事支出，必須提高生產效率、改善產品組合，或調高商品與服務價格。然而，這些調整並非所有企業都能順利完成，尤其在市場競爭激烈、成本轉嫁能力不足的情況下，薪資上漲可能進一步侵蝕利潤。
東京商工調查統計，今年4月至9月，日本因人手不足而破產的企業達240家，年增17%，創該公司同期調查以來新高。
其中，因人工成本上漲而破產的企業達130家，年增75.6%，占缺工相關破產案件逾半。

日本殭屍企業約25.1萬家　低利率環境難以持續支撐

第三項壓力來自日本長期存在的低獲利、高負債的大量「殭屍企業」，失去了利率緩衝。
過去多年，日本維持超低利率環境，加上疫情期間提供的零利率、零擔保貸款，部分財務體質不佳的企業得以延續營運；隨著利率上升，這些企業的償債壓力也逐漸加重。
所謂「殭屍企業」，依國際清算銀行的定義，是指成立10年以上，且連續3年利息保障倍數低於1的企業，也就是營業利潤不足以支付利息支出。
帝國資料銀行上半年統計指出，日本目前約有25.1萬家殭屍企業，占全國企業總數17.1%。
對這類企業而言，利率變動可能帶來遠高於帳面數字的衝擊。相關研究的壓力測試顯示，若企業借款利率上升0.25個百分點，平均每家殭屍企業每年將增加約64萬日元的利息負擔。
即使增加的金額看似有限，對於原本獲利不足以支付利息、且缺乏充足現金與資本緩衝的企業而言，仍可能進一步壓縮償還本金、更新設備及維持日常營運的空間。
若日本持續升息，企業財務風險可能進一步擴大，並透過貸款違約與不良債權增加，傳導至銀行體系。不過，破產案件增加是否會演變成大規模銀行壞帳問題，仍取決於企業違約程度、銀行放款曝險及後續金融環境變化。

企業反對升息聲浪增加　日本央行仍須顧及通膨

面對企業經營壓力升高，日本央行的貨幣政策也陷入兩難。
東京商工調查今年2月針對5,170家企業進行調查，59.6%的受訪企業希望未來一年維持政策利率不變，另有23.6%希望降息。原文指出，當時政策利率為0.75%，目前已升至1.25%。
企業希望維持較低利率，主要是為了減輕融資成本，避免利息支出排擠設備投資與日常營運資金。然而，若日本央行因企業破產增加而過早停止升息，也可能面臨日元再度走弱、進口成本居高不下的風險。
從整體中小企業的融資狀況來看，目前尚未出現普遍性的資金緊縮。10月1日公布的調查顯示，中小企業資金週轉判斷指數為正8，銀行貸款態度判斷指數為正12，兩項指數均與6月持平，反映整體企業的資金狀況仍未全面惡化。
另一方面，日本物價壓力也尚未完全消退。
日本8月剔除生鮮食品的核心消費者物價指數（CPI）年增1.7%，剔除生鮮食品與能源後的指數則年增1.9%。
與此同時，日本央行公布的數據顯示，8月國內企業物價指數年增7.6%，以日元計價的進口物價指數年增24.8%。
儘管兩項指數當月分別月減0.2%與3.0%，企業採購成本仍明顯高於一年前。若日元再度走弱，能源與原物料進口成本可能進一步增加，使企業面臨更大的成本轉嫁壓力。
日本企業對未來物價的預期同樣值得關注。9月調查顯示，企業預期未來1年及3年的一般物價平均年增率均為2.6%，5年後則為2.5%。
以未來1年通膨預期作為參考，若政策利率為1.25%，扣除2.6%的預期通膨率後，實質政策利率約為負1.35%。
日本央行因此仍須評估，若工資、商品價格與通膨預期持續相互推升，是否需要進一步調整利率，以避免物價漲勢變得更加持久。
原文引述9月會議意見摘要指出，在物價朝政策目標發展、金融條件仍寬鬆的情況下，應持續調整利率；若物價出現向上偏離目標的跡象，也可能需要加快調整步伐。
這意味著，企業破產增加雖然構成政策考量，但未必足以讓日本央行立即停止升息。未來政策走向仍將取決於通膨、匯率及整體融資環境的變化。

升息0.5個百分點　虧損企業比率恐進一步攀升

企業面臨的財務壓力，還可能隨著既有貸款利率調整而逐步浮現，即使日本央行放慢升息速度，企業仍須承擔先前利率調整的後續影響。
東京商工調查今年8月公布一項研究，以321,953家具有付息負債的中小企業2025年財務數據為基礎，在其他財務條件不變的假設下，模擬利率上升對企業獲利的影響。
結果顯示，若利率上升0.5個百分點，虧損企業占比將由27.7%升至29.4%；若上升1個百分點，虧損企業占比則將達31.0%。依公布比例粗略推算，兩種情境下，樣本中的虧損企業淨增加數量分別約為5,500家及1.06萬家。
這項模擬顯示，利率上升可能使原本僅有微薄利潤的企業轉為虧損，也會進一步加重既有虧損企業的財務負擔。不過，這是建立在其他財務條件不變下的情境分析，並不代表實際破產數量必然增加相同幅度。
此外，帝國資料銀行估計，日本殭屍企業中，同時面臨經常性虧損、過度負債及資不抵債三項問題的企業約有3.6萬家，占殭屍企業總數17.2%。這些企業的獲利與資本緩衝本就不足，若利息支出持續增加，將更難維持資金週轉。
貸款利率調整的影響也正逐步傳導。9月調查顯示，中小企業借款利率判斷指數由6月的正61升至正70，代表相較於回報利率下降的企業，回報借款利率上升的企業占據更明顯優勢。
由於貸款利率調整與到期續借並非同時發生，過去升息的影響仍可能在未來數季陸續反映於企業財務報表。

日本企業破產風險仍待觀察　央行面臨政策兩難

綜合企業破產、成本轉嫁能力、勞動力短缺與利率壓力等因素，日本未來數季的企業破產案件仍存在增加風險，尤其是現金儲備有限、利息保障倍數偏低，且難以將成本轉嫁給客戶的企業。
後續企業經營環境能否改善，將取決於多項條件，包括進口成本是否下降、企業調價能力是否提升，以及債務重整能否降低還款負擔。
即使日本央行暫停升息，企業已經累積的債務與成本壓力也不會立即消失；反之，若持續升息，則可能進一步壓縮企業利潤與現金流。
對日本央行而言，政策難題在於如何兼顧物價穩定與企業財務韌性：升息可能加快部分企業的償債問題浮現，但若過早停止緊縮，日元與進口物價壓力又可能重新增加企業負擔。
日本企業破產案件創下13年同期新高，反映出在低利率環境逐步退場之際，企業財務體質差異正變得更加明顯。未來升息的實際影響，除了取決於政策利率調整幅度，也將受到貸款重新定價速度、企業現金儲備及整體經營環境左右。
paras_en: Japanese monetary policy is tightening gradually, and corporate operating pressures are rising steadily. Data from the Tokyo Shoko Research company recently released shows that in the first half of the 2026 fiscal year (April to September), there were 5,373 bankruptcy cases of companies with liabilities exceeding 10 million yen, a 3.8% year‑on‑year increase, reaching a 13‑year high for the same period; the total debt of bankruptcies reached 856.169 billion yen, up 23.5% from the previous year.
From a size perspective, 77% of the bankruptcies involved companies with liabilities under 100 million yen, and 90.6% involved companies with fewer than 10 employees.
In addition, traditional Japanese companies are not immune. From January to August this year, 112 companies that had been established for over a century entered legal bankruptcy proceedings.

Analysts point out that this wave of corporate failures is not only due to higher financing costs from rising rates, but also to increases in raw material and wage costs, labor shortages, and the debt pressure faced by companies that have long relied on low interest rates to sustain operations.
As the Bank of Japan continues to advance monetary policy normalization, the financial fragility of companies is gradually surfacing.
Japanese companies face triple pressure: rising rates exacerbate the funding difficulties of small and medium‑sized enterprises.
Bankruptcies among Japanese companies continue to rise, mainly due to three factors, with rising rates pushing up funding costs, a key reason for increased operating pressure.

Companies often have a certain cash‑flow cycle from purchasing raw materials, paying wages, completing orders, and collecting payments. When internal funds are insufficient, companies must rely on bank loans to meet operational needs, so an increase in borrowing rates directly raises their funding costs.

More importantly, raw material and wage costs rise together, requiring companies to prepare more working capital. If product sales slow or customers delay payments, companies not only face higher interest expenses but also longer periods of capital tied up, further increasing financial burden.

When profitability declines and debt‑servicing ability weakens, banks may also reassess lending risk, raising the cost of new loans and creating a vicious cycle of operating pressure and financing difficulty.

Tokyo Shoko Research data shows that in the first half of the 2026 fiscal year, 436 companies went bankrupt due to price increases, a 17.8% year‑on‑year rise; among them, 63.9% had capital under 10 million yen, indicating that smaller capital firms are more vulnerable to cost shocks.

Another key factor is the limited ability of companies to pass costs onto customers. Teikoku Databank surveyed 10,518 companies in July this year, finding that the overall cost‑passing rate for Japanese companies was only 39.9%, and the restaurant sector only 28.7%; only 3.4% of companies could fully pass on new costs.
The aging population exacerbates labor shortages, and rising labor costs are one of the main reasons for bankruptcies.

In September, the Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications reported that 29.6% of the population is aged 65 or older, a historical high. Teikoku Databank’s July survey also found that 51.3% of surveyed companies reported insufficient full‑time staff, showing that labor shortages remain widespread.
For companies, labor shortages not only limit production and order‑taking capacity but also force them to raise wages to attract and retain staff.
From October 2026, Japan has been gradually adjusting minimum wages nationwide, with the weighted average hourly wage reaching 1,177 yen, up 56 yen from the previous year, a 5% increase.

To absorb higher personnel costs, companies must improve production efficiency, adjust product mix, or raise prices. However, not all companies can implement these adjustments smoothly, especially in highly competitive markets with limited cost‑passing ability, so wage increases may further erode profits.

Tokyo Shoko Research statistics show that from April to September this year, 240 companies went bankrupt due to labor shortages, a 17% year‑on‑year increase, a new high for the company’s same‑period survey.
Among them, 130 companies went bankrupt due to rising labor costs, a 75.6% increase, accounting for more than half of labor‑shortage‑related bankruptcies.
Japanese zombie companies number about 251,000, and the low‑interest‑rate environment can no longer sustain them.
The third pressure comes from the long‑existing large number of low‑profit, high‑debt zombie companies that have lost the interest‑rate buffer.

For many years, Japan maintained an ultra‑low‑interest‑rate environment, and during the pandemic, zero‑interest, zero‑guarantee loans allowed some financially weak companies to continue operating; as rates rise, these companies’ debt‑servicing pressure gradually increases.

A “zombie company” is defined by the International Liquidation Bank as a company that has existed for more than ten years and has had an interest‑coverage ratio below one for three consecutive years, meaning operating profit is insufficient to cover interest expenses.
Teikoku Databank’s first‑half statistics indicate that Japan currently has about 251,000 zombie companies, accounting for 17.1% of all companies nationwide.

For these companies, interest rate changes can have impacts far beyond the book value. Stress tests show that if borrowing rates rise by 0.25 percentage points, each zombie company will face an additional 640,000 yen of interest burden per year on average.

Even though the additional amount seems modest, for companies that already cannot cover interest, lack sufficient cash and capital buffers, it can further squeeze the space for principal repayment, equipment renewal, and day‑to‑day operations.

If Japan continues to raise rates, corporate financial risk may expand further, leading to increased loan defaults and non‑performing loans that transmit to the banking system. However, whether the rise in bankruptcies will evolve into a large‑scale banking bad‑loan problem still depends on the degree of corporate defaults, banks’ lending exposure, and subsequent changes in the financial environment.
Corporate opposition to rate hikes is growing, and the Bank of Japan must still consider inflation.
Facing rising corporate operating pressures, the Bank of Japan’s monetary policy is in a dilemma.

In February, Tokyo Shoko Research surveyed 5,170 companies, finding that 59.6% of respondents wanted the policy rate to remain unchanged for the next year, and 23.6% wanted a rate cut. At that time, the policy rate was 0.75%, now 1.25%.

Companies want to keep rates low mainly to reduce financing costs and avoid interest expenses crowding out equipment investment and working capital. However, if the Bank of Japan stops raising rates too early due to increased bankruptcies, it may face a renewed weakening of the yen and persistently high import costs.

Looking at the overall SME financing situation, there is no widespread tightening of funds yet. A survey released on October 1 shows that the SME cash‑flow judgment index is +8, and the bank lending attitude index is +12, both unchanged from June, indicating that overall corporate funding conditions have not deteriorated significantly.
On the other hand, Japan’s price pressure has not fully eased.
In August, Japan’s core CPI excluding fresh food rose 1.7% year‑on‑year; the CPI excluding fresh food and energy rose 1.9% year‑on‑year.
Meanwhile, the Bank of Japan’s data shows that in August, the domestic enterprise price index rose 7.6% year‑on‑year, and the import price index in yen rose 24.8% year‑on‑year.

Although both indices fell 0.2% and 3.0% respectively that month, companies’ procurement costs remain clearly higher than a year ago. If the yen weakens again, energy and raw‑material import costs may rise further, increasing the pressure on companies to pass costs on.

Japanese companies’ expectations for future prices are also worth noting. A September survey showed that companies expect the average annual inflation rate for the next 1 and 3 years to be 2.6%, and 2.5% after five years.

Using the 1‑year inflation expectation as a reference, if the policy rate is 1.25% and the expected inflation is 2.6%, the real policy rate is about –1.35%.
The Bank of Japan therefore still needs to assess whether, if wages, product prices, and inflation expectations continue to push each other up, further rate adjustments are needed to prevent inflation from becoming more persistent.

The original text cites a September meeting summary stating that as prices move toward the policy target and financial conditions remain loose, rates should continue to be adjusted; if prices show upward bias away from the target, the pace of adjustment may need to accelerate.

This means that while an increase in bankruptcies is a policy consideration, it may not be enough for the Bank of Japan to immediately stop raising rates. Future policy direction will still depend on changes in inflation, exchange rates, and the overall financing environment.
A 0.5 percentage‑point rate hike could further raise the proportion of loss‑making companies.

Corporate financial pressure may also gradually surface as existing loan rates adjust; even if the Bank of Japan slows its rate hikes, companies still face the aftereffects of previous rate adjustments.

In August, Tokyo Shoko Research released a study based on the 2025 financial data of 321,953 SMEs with interest‑bearing debt, assuming other financial conditions remain unchanged, simulating the impact of rate increases on profitability.

The results show that if rates rise by 0.5 percentage points, the share of loss‑making companies will rise from 27.7% to 29.4%; if rates rise by 1 percentage point, the share will reach 31.0%. Roughly estimating based on the published proportions, the net increase in loss‑making companies in the sample would be about 5,500 and 10,600 respectively.

This simulation shows that rate increases could turn marginally profitable companies into loss‑making ones and further burden existing loss‑making companies. However, this is a scenario analysis assuming other financial conditions remain unchanged and does not necessarily mean actual bankruptcies will increase by the same magnitude.

Teikoku Databank estimates that among zombie companies, about 36,000 face the three problems of ongoing losses, excessive debt, and insufficient asset coverage, accounting for 17.2% of all zombie companies. These companies already have insufficient profitability and capital buffers, and if interest expenses continue to rise, they will find it even harder to maintain cash flow.

The impact of loan rate adjustments is gradually transmitting. A September survey shows that the SME loan rate judgment index rose from +61 in June to +70, indicating that compared to firms whose return rates have fallen, firms whose borrowing rates have risen have a more pronounced advantage.
Because loan rate adjustments and maturity roll‑overs do not occur simultaneously, the impact of past rate hikes may still reflect in corporate financial statements over the next few quarters.
Japanese corporate bankruptcy risk remains to be observed, and the central bank faces a policy dilemma.

Combining corporate bankruptcies, cost‑passing ability, labor shortages, and interest‑rate pressure, the risk of increased bankruptcies in the coming quarters remains, especially for companies with limited cash reserves, low interest‑coverage ratios, and difficulty passing costs to customers.

Whether the corporate operating environment improves will depend on multiple factors, including whether import costs fall, whether companies can raise prices, and whether debt restructuring can reduce repayment burdens.
Even if the Bank of Japan pauses rate hikes, accumulated debt and cost pressure will not disappear immediately; conversely, continued rate hikes may further squeeze corporate profits and cash flow.
For the Bank of Japan, the policy challenge is how to balance price stability and corporate financial resilience: rate hikes may accelerate the emergence of debt problems for some companies, but stopping tightening too early may again increase yen weakness and import price pressure, adding to corporate burden.
Japanese corporate bankruptcies reach a 13‑year high for the same period, reflecting that as the low‑rate environment gradually exits, differences in corporate financial health are becoming more pronounced. The actual impact of future rate hikes will depend not only on the magnitude of policy rate adjustments but also on the speed of loan repricing, corporate cash reserves, and the overall operating environment.

items.title: 遞延訂單回補！裕慶-KY 9月營收月增75% 第4季營運有望回溫
items.title_en: Deferred Orders Rebound! Yucheng-KY September Revenue Up 75%; Q4 Operations Expected to Warm Up
paras: 裕慶-KY(6957-TW)配合美國零售通路改裝時程，第三季營收連續2個月處於相對低檔，不過9月營運明顯回溫。裕慶-KY今(11)日公布最新營收，2026年9月營收回升至4.29億元，較8月的2.45億元大增75.29%，年增43.98%；2026年1至9月累計營收達30.07億元，年增12.46%。
裕慶-KY第三季營收爲8.96億元，季減18.78，探5季以來新低點，年減17.47%。
裕慶-KY在7月及8月營收主要受到部分大型零售客戶配合新開店及門市改裝時程調整，導致部分商用展示架專案訂單遞延至9月起陸續加速出貨與認列。惟觀察北美零售市場需求依舊強勁，包括Lowe’s、CVS等客戶近期陸續增加展店計畫，加上既有門市汰換及空間升級需求同步推進，商用展示架訂單需求仍維持熱絡，甚至出現商用展示架急單湧現情況。
裕慶-KY為全力配合客戶交期與訂單需求，已規劃啟動三班式生產模式提高產能調配彈性，若相關遞延訂單與急單順利拉貨認列，將有助商用展示架出貨規模明顯放大，可望進一步帶動第四季營運動能進一步升溫。
隨著大型零售通路持續強化商品陳列、品牌專區及全通路履約功能，商用展示架需求已由新店開設，進一步延伸至既有門市汰舊換新、品類重整及數位設備整合。另一方面，美國零售業者亦加速導入電子貨架標籤、庫存感測及數位揀貨設備，帶動展示架朝智能化與高附加價值方向升級。
裕慶-KY持續掌握智慧零售及門市數位化趨勢，推動商用展示架朝高附加價值方向發展，裕慶-KY旗下智慧電子標籤展示架已陸續出貨，並同步投入新一代產品開發，透過整合電子資訊顯示、智慧化管理及零售場域應用等功能，進一步提升產品附加價值，新產品預計於今年底前完成客戶測試與認證，後續隨客戶導入進度推進，可望逐步擴大智慧零售產品線的營運貢獻。
paras_en: Yucheng-KY (6957-TW) has seen its third‑quarter revenue stay at a relatively low level for two consecutive months while aligning with the U.S. retail outlet renovation schedule, but operations clearly improved in September. The company announced today (Nov. 11) that September 2026 revenue rose to NT$429 million, a 75.29% jump from August’s NT$245 million and a 43.98% year‑over‑year increase; cumulative revenue for January‑September 2026 reached NT$3.007 billion, up 12.46% YoY.
Yucheng-KY’s third‑quarter revenue was NT$896 million, down 18.78% quarter‑on‑quarter, hitting a five‑quarter low, and down 17.47% year‑on‑year.

In July and August, Yucheng-KY’s revenue was mainly affected by several large retail customers adjusting their new‑store openings and store‑renovation schedules, causing some commercial display‑rack project orders to be deferred and then gradually accelerated for shipment and recognition starting in September. Nevertheless, demand in the North American retail market remains strong, with customers such as Lowe’s and CVS recently expanding store‑opening plans, and ongoing replacement and space‑upgrade projects at existing stores keeping commercial display‑rack orders robust, even leading to a surge of urgent orders.

To fully meet customer delivery timelines and order needs, Yucheng-KY has planned to launch a three‑shift production mode to increase capacity‑allocation flexibility. If the deferred and urgent orders are successfully shipped and recognized, the scale of commercial display‑rack shipments could expand markedly, further boosting fourth‑quarter operational momentum.

As major retail channels continue to strengthen product merchandising, brand zones, and omnichannel fulfillment capabilities, demand for commercial display racks has shifted from new‑store openings to include replacement of existing stores, category restructuring, and digital equipment integration. Meanwhile, U.S. retailers are accelerating the adoption of electronic shelf labels, inventory sensing, and digital picking equipment, driving display racks toward smarter, higher‑value solutions.

Yucheng-KY continues to capture the smart‑retail and store‑digitalization trends, advancing commercial display racks toward higher value. Its smart electronic‑label display racks have been shipped progressively, and the company is investing in next‑generation product development. By integrating electronic information display, intelligent management, and retail‑site applications, product value is further enhanced. The new product is expected to complete customer testing and certification by year‑end, and as customers roll out the solution, it should gradually expand the contribution of the smart‑retail product line to operations.

items.title: 胡塞武裝稱「已關閉利雅得機場」！沙國防空飛彈告急、川普稱美「有可能」加入打擊
items.title_en: Houthi Forces Claim 'Riyadh Airport Closed'! Saudi Air‑Defense Missiles Running Low, Trump Says US 'May' Join Strikes
paras: 葉門胡塞武裝與沙烏地阿拉伯衝突升溫，沙國首都利雅德國際機場10日遭襲，造成12死、309傷，胡塞武裝11日更警告航空業者與旅客避開沙國機場。沙國防空攔截飛彈庫存告急，正尋求多國支援；美國總統川普則表示，美國可能加入沙國對胡塞武裝的打擊行動。隨著葉門多座機場接連遇襲，區域航空安全與人道局勢面臨更大風險。
沙烏地阿拉伯首都利雅德的哈立德國王國際機場遭襲後，胡塞武裝控制的薩巴通訊社負責人阿米爾（Nasruddin Amer）在社群媒體發文，宣稱利雅德國際機場已遭關閉。
胡塞武裝並指責沙國未能成功攔截攻擊，應為此負責。該組織此前也曾要求民航機避開沙國領空，並將沙國領空列為軍事行動區。
據《美聯社》11日報導，多名沙國官員表示，沙國防空攔截飛彈庫存已面臨短缺，並已向法國、英國、巴基斯坦及埃及尋求支援，希望相關國家在當地部署防空系統。
其中一名官員指出，美國在與伊朗的戰事中，同樣面臨武器庫存持續消耗的問題。
沙國官員並透露，美方提供的支援包括情報共享、目標辨識，以及協助規劃近期針對胡塞武裝的攻勢。
沙國主導的多國聯軍發言人馬利基（Turki Al-Maliki）11日在社群媒體表示，胡塞武裝10日襲擊哈立德國王國際機場的一座航廈，造成旅客及機場工作人員傷亡。
他將這起事件定性為「恐怖攻擊」，並稱其構成戰爭罪，強調聯軍將予以堅決回應。
馬利基此前也表示，聯軍已攔截並摧毀胡塞武裝朝利雅德東南方海爾季市（Al-Kharj）發射的一枚彈道飛彈。
沙國民航部門11日凌晨公布，機場遇襲事件共造成12人死亡、309人受傷。死者包括4名沙國公民、2名孟加拉國公民，以及分別來自美國、埃及、約旦、敘利亞、巴勒斯坦與蘇丹的6人。
爆炸發生後，航班追蹤網站顯示，利雅德機場一度沒有航班起降，部分飛往當地的航班改降其他機場或折返。機場方面也提醒旅客，出發前應先聯繫航空公司，確認航班最新狀態。
美國總統川普10日針對機場遇襲事件發表聲明，表示，美國「可能」加入沙烏地阿拉伯針對胡塞武裝的打擊行動，「我們將仔細考慮」，並未明確承諾出兵。
有分析認為，美國對直接打擊胡塞武裝態度審慎，與當前對伊朗戰事尚未結束、武器庫存因戰事大量消耗且尚未補充有關。在現階段的戰略考量下，保護沙國並非美國的首要任務，美方因此不願進一步開闢葉門戰線。

葉門多座機場接連遇襲　衝突擴大至民航設施

葉門衝突近期延燒至民航設施。過去一週，沙國利雅德國際機場、由葉門政府軍控制的亞丁國際機場，以及胡塞武裝控制區內的薩那國際機場與荷台達國際機場，接連傳出遇襲事件。
其中，薩那與荷台達機場是國際航班及人道援助物資進入胡塞武裝控制區的重要通道。胡塞武裝攻擊沙國機場，被視為對相關衝突採取的對等反制行動。
有美方分析指出，沙國近期正值會議及旅遊旺季，胡塞武裝攻擊利雅德機場，可能意在威脅沙國的商業活動與觀光產業。
另一方面，亞丁機場是葉門南部少數仍可使用的國際航空門戶，若持續遭到攻擊，恐進一步惡化葉門政府控制區的人道局勢。
葉門政府10日警告，胡塞武裝對亞丁國際機場的打擊，顯示其戰術出現「關鍵轉變」。
paras_en: The conflict between Yemen's Houthi forces and Saudi Arabia has intensified, with Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport hit on the 10th, killing 12 and injuring 309. On the 11th the Houthis warned airlines and passengers to avoid Saudi airports. Saudi air‑defence missile stocks are critically low and the kingdom is seeking multilateral assistance; U.S. President Donald Trump said the United States might join Saudi actions against the Houthis. As several Yemeni airports have also been struck, regional aviation safety and humanitarian conditions face heightened risk.

After the attack on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, Nasruddin Amer, head of the Houthi‑controlled Saba News Agency, posted on social media that Riyadh’s international airport had been closed.

The Houthis also blamed Saudi Arabia for failing to intercept the attack and said it should be held responsible. The group had previously urged civil aviation to steer clear of Saudi airspace and declared Saudi airspace a military operations zone.

According to an Associated Press report on the 11th, multiple Saudi officials said the kingdom’s air‑defence missile inventory is running short and that they have asked France, the United Kingdom, Pakistan and Egypt for support, hoping those countries will deploy air‑defence systems on site.
One official noted that the United States is facing a similar depletion of its weapons stockpiles in its ongoing conflict with Iran.
Saudi officials also disclosed that U.S. assistance includes intelligence sharing, target identification, and help planning a near‑term offensive against the Houthis.

Turki Al‑Maliki, the spokesperson for the Saudi‑led multinational coalition, posted on social media on the 11th that the Houthi attack on the 10th hit a terminal at King Khalid International Airport, causing casualties among passengers and airport staff.
He classified the incident as a "terrorist attack" and said it constituted a war crime, stressing that the coalition would respond resolutely.
Maliki previously said the coalition had intercepted and destroyed a ballistic missile the Houthis launched toward Al‑Kharj, a city southeast of Riyadh.

Saudi civil aviation authorities announced in the early hours of the 11th that the airport attack resulted in 12 deaths and 309 injuries. The dead included four Saudi citizens, two Bangladeshis, and six others from the United States, Egypt, Jordan, Syria, Palestine and Sudan.

After the explosion, flight‑tracking sites showed that Riyadh Airport temporarily had no take‑offs or landings; some flights bound for the city were diverted to other airports or turned back. The airport urged passengers to contact their airlines before departure to confirm the latest flight status.

President Donald Trump issued a statement on the 10th regarding the airport attack, saying the United States "may" join Saudi Arabia’s strike against the Houthis and that "we will consider it carefully," without committing troops.

Analysts believe the U.S. is cautious about directly striking the Houthis because the war with Iran is still ongoing and U.S. weapon stocks have been heavily depleted and not yet replenished. Under current strategic considerations, protecting Saudi Arabia is not a top U.S. priority, so Washington is reluctant to open a new front in Yemen.

Yemen’s conflict has recently spread to civil aviation facilities. In the past week, Riyadh International Airport, Aden International Airport (controlled by Yemen’s government forces), and the Houthi‑controlled Sana’a and Hodeidah airports have all reported attacks.

Sana’a and Hodeidah airports are key gateways for international flights and humanitarian aid entering Houthi‑controlled areas. Houthi attacks on Saudi airports are seen as reciprocal actions in the broader conflict.

U.S. analysts note that Saudi Arabia is currently in a peak conference and tourism season, and the Houthi strike on Riyadh Airport may be intended to threaten Saudi commercial activity and its tourism industry.

Meanwhile, Aden Airport is one of the few remaining international aviation gateways in southern Yemen; continued attacks could further worsen the humanitarian situation in government‑controlled areas.
The Yemeni government warned on the 10th that the Houthi strike on Aden International Airport signals a "critical shift" in their tactics.

items.title: 遞延訂單回補！裕慶-KY 9月營收月增75% 第4季營運有望回溫
items.title_en: Deferred Orders Rebound! Yucheng-KY September Revenue Up 75%; Q4 Operations Expected to Warm Up
paras: 裕慶-KY(6957-TW)配合美國零售通路改裝時程，第三季營收連續2個月處於相對低檔，不過9月營運明顯回溫。裕慶-KY今(11)日公布最新營收，2026年9月營收回升至4.29億元，較8月的2.45億元大增75.29%，年增43.98%；2026年1至9月累計營收達30.07億元，年增12.46%。
裕慶-KY第三季營收爲8.96億元，季減18.78，探5季以來新低點，年減17.47%。
裕慶-KY在7月及8月營收主要受到部分大型零售客戶配合新開店及門市改裝時程調整，導致部分商用展示架專案訂單遞延至9月起陸續加速出貨與認列。惟觀察北美零售市場需求依舊強勁，包括Lowe’s、CVS等客戶近期陸續增加展店計畫，加上既有門市汰換及空間升級需求同步推進，商用展示架訂單需求仍維持熱絡，甚至出現商用展示架急單湧現情況。
裕慶-KY為全力配合客戶交期與訂單需求，已規劃啟動三班式生產模式提高產能調配彈性，若相關遞延訂單與急單順利拉貨認列，將有助商用展示架出貨規模明顯放大，可望進一步帶動第四季營運動能進一步升溫。
隨著大型零售通路持續強化商品陳列、品牌專區及全通路履約功能，商用展示架需求已由新店開設，進一步延伸至既有門市汰舊換新、品類重整及數位設備整合。另一方面，美國零售業者亦加速導入電子貨架標籤、庫存感測及數位揀貨設備，帶動展示架朝智能化與高附加價值方向升級。
裕慶-KY持續掌握智慧零售及門市數位化趨勢，推動商用展示架朝高附加價值方向發展，裕慶-KY旗下智慧電子標籤展示架已陸續出貨，並同步投入新一代產品開發，透過整合電子資訊顯示、智慧化管理及零售場域應用等功能，進一步提升產品附加價值，新產品預計於今年底前完成客戶測試與認證，後續隨客戶導入進度推進，可望逐步擴大智慧零售產品線的營運貢獻。
paras_en: Yucheng-KY (6957-TW) has seen its third‑quarter revenue stay at a relatively low level for two consecutive months while aligning with the U.S. retail outlet renovation schedule, but operations clearly improved in September. The company announced today (Nov. 11) that September 2026 revenue rose to NT$429 million, a 75.29% jump from August’s NT$245 million and a 43.98% year‑over‑year increase; cumulative revenue for January‑September 2026 reached NT$3.007 billion, up 12.46% YoY.
Yucheng-KY’s third‑quarter revenue was NT$896 million, down 18.78% quarter‑on‑quarter, hitting a five‑quarter low, and down 17.47% year‑on‑year.

In July and August, Yucheng-KY’s revenue was mainly affected by several large retail customers adjusting their new‑store openings and store‑renovation schedules, causing some commercial display‑rack project orders to be deferred and then gradually accelerated for shipment and recognition starting in September. Nevertheless, demand in the North American retail market remains strong, with customers such as Lowe’s and CVS recently expanding store‑opening plans, and ongoing replacement and space‑upgrade projects at existing stores keeping commercial display‑rack orders robust, even leading to a surge of urgent orders.

To fully meet customer delivery timelines and order needs, Yucheng-KY has planned to launch a three‑shift production mode to increase capacity‑allocation flexibility. If the deferred and urgent orders are successfully shipped and recognized, the scale of commercial display‑rack shipments could expand markedly, further boosting fourth‑quarter operational momentum.

As major retail channels continue to strengthen product merchandising, brand zones, and omnichannel fulfillment capabilities, demand for commercial display racks has shifted from new‑store openings to include replacement of existing stores, category restructuring, and digital equipment integration. Meanwhile, U.S. retailers are accelerating the adoption of electronic shelf labels, inventory sensing, and digital picking equipment, driving display racks toward smarter, higher‑value solutions.

Yucheng-KY continues to capture the smart‑retail and store‑digitalization trends, advancing commercial display racks toward higher value. Its smart electronic‑label display racks have been shipped progressively, and the company is investing in next‑generation product development. By integrating electronic information display, intelligent management, and retail‑site applications, product value is further enhanced. The new product is expected to complete customer testing and certification by year‑end, and as customers roll out the solution, it should gradually expand the contribution of the smart‑retail product line to operations.

items.title: 鴻海及子公司遭美國337調查 強調營運出貨正常、已組團隊釐清因應
items.title_en: Foxconn and Subsidiaries Subject to US 337 Investigation, Emphasize Operations and Shipments Remain Normal, Team Assembled to Clarify Response
paras: 美國國際貿易委員會（USITC）於美國時間2026年10月9日，就美國電源供應模組廠商Vicor Corporation提出的專利侵權主張，正式啟動337調查（調查編號：337-TA-1526），包括台達電(2308-TW)、鴻海(2317-TW)、廣達(2382-TW)等多家台廠及其關係企業被列為被調查方。
據了解，本次調查涉及美國專利US 10,903,734，調查範圍涵蓋特定垂直供電系統、相關組件，以及搭載該等系統的運算系統。鴻海及相關企業工業富聯(FII)(601138-CN)、FII USA Inc.、鴻佰科技（Ingrasys Technology Inc.）及Ingrasys Technology USA Inc.等均被列為調查對象。
鴻海發出聲明指出，經初步評估，本次調查目前未對公司及相關企業的生產營運、產品出貨及客戶合作造成重大影響，營運維持正常，並將持續與客戶及供應鏈合作夥伴保持溝通，公司尊重智慧財產權，已組成專業團隊釐清相關專利及產品範圍，並將依照法定程序積極應對，以維護公司及股東權益。
鴻海進一步指出，本案目前仍處於立案初期，USITC僅決定啟動調查，尚未就Vicor Corporation提出的侵權主張作出任何實質認定，由於本案後續結果仍存在不確定性，公司將密切關注調查進展及可能影響，並依相關法令辦理資訊揭露。
paras_en: On October 9, 2026 (U.S. time), the U.S. International Trade Commission (USITC) formally launched a Section 337 investigation (investigation number 337-TA-1526) in response to a patent‑infringement claim filed by American power‑module maker Vicor Corporation. The investigation lists several Taiwanese companies and their affiliates—including Delta Electronics (2308‑TW), Foxconn (2317‑TW) and Quanta Computer (2382‑TW)—as respondents.

The probe concerns U.S. Patent No. 10,903,734 and covers specific vertical power‑delivery systems, related components, and computing systems that incorporate those systems. Foxconn and related firms such as Foxconn Industrial Internet (FII) (601138‑CN), FII USA Inc., Ingrasys Technology Inc. and Ingrasys Technology USA Inc. are among those named in the investigation.

Foxconn issued a statement saying that, based on a preliminary assessment, the investigation has not yet had a material impact on the company’s or its affiliates’ production operations, product shipments or customer collaborations. Operations remain normal, and the company will continue communicating with customers and supply‑chain partners. Foxconn respects intellectual‑property rights, has formed a professional team to clarify the relevant patents and product scope, and will actively respond through the legal process to protect the interests of the company and its shareholders.

Foxconn added that the case is still in its early filing stage; the USITC has only decided to open the investigation and has not made any substantive finding on Vicor’s infringement allegations. Because the ultimate outcome remains uncertain, the company will closely monitor the investigation’s progress and any potential impacts, and will disclose information in accordance with applicable regulations.

items.title: 大盤創高後拉回 這12檔台股ETF規模仍創高 00927今年來漲幅翻倍居冠
items.title_en: Market Hits Highs Then Pulls Back, Yet 12 Taiwan Stock ETFs Still Reach Record Sizes; 00927 Doubles Gains This Year
paras: 大盤創高後拉回整理，但仍有台股ETF規模逆勢創高，根據CMONEY統計資料顯示，包括群益半導體收益(00927-TW)、國泰永續高股息(00878-TW)、元大高股息(0056-TW)在內有12檔規模創新高，其中以市值、高息型為主。進一步觀察這12檔今年以來含息績效表現，以群益 00927 上漲107.36%翻倍的績效居冠。
據了解，00927 群益半導體收益ETF每1、4、7、10月配息，成分股皆為享譽全球的半導體供應鏈大廠，整體持股布局橫跨IC設計、晶圓代工與製造、封裝測試等領域，完整涵蓋半導體產業生態系，主要集中在先進製程與成熟代工(台積電、聯電、日月光)，同時搭配傳統高息股(如瑞昱)，兼具半導體與高息兩大市場火熱主題，有助投資人把握半導體產業成長行情，還能兼顧收益需求。
群益投信台股研究團隊表示，國人熱愛台股ETF是因為其波動度相對個股與大盤來的低，現階段大盤頻創新高下，接下來面臨的挑戰更為複雜，台股類股輪動快速、個股波動性大，預期台股指數傾向高檔震盪，建議投資人可以透過高股息ETF來為投組增加抗震力，其中結合半導體科技產業成長前景的高股息ETF除了具低波動特性、可兼顧收益需求，還有AI熱潮所帶來的潛在資本利得可期，因此成為現階段資金配置的最佳選擇。

群益半導體收益 ETF 經理人謝明志表示，台股高股息ETF的特性偏向高配息兼具成長性的股票，涵蓋全產業配置能兼顧多元產業紅利，而台灣半導體8月營收年增61%大幅優於歷史平均，第三季在AI先進製程與高階封測驅動下，晶圓代工與封測營收預估季增15%至20%。第四季受惠旺季動能延續，族群營收料維持雙位數季增。台灣作為AI產業關鍵供應鏈，不論是先進代工、封裝等半導體電子產業相關供應鏈營運有望持續受惠，台股盤勢仍有望迎接第四季傳統股市旺季上漲契機。

paras_en: After the market hit new highs and then retreated for a pull‑back, Taiwan stock ETFs continued to grow against the trend. According to CMONEY data, twelve ETFs—including Qunyi Semiconductor Yield (00927‑TW), Cathay Sustainable High Dividend (00878‑TW) and Yuanta High Dividend (0056‑TW)—set new record assets, mainly large‑cap and high‑yield funds. Looking at their total‑return performance since the start of the year, Qunyi’s 00927 led with a 107.36% rise, effectively doubling its value.

The 00927 Qunyi Semiconductor Yield ETF distributes dividends in January, April, July and October. Its holdings consist of globally renowned semiconductor supply‑chain giants, spanning IC design, wafer foundry, manufacturing and packaging/testing, covering the entire semiconductor ecosystem. The portfolio focuses on advanced and mature fabs such as TSMC, UMC and ASE, while also including traditional high‑yield stocks like Realtek, blending semiconductor growth with high‑dividend themes to let investors capture industry expansion while meeting income needs.

Qunyi Asset Management’s Taiwan equity research team notes that Taiwanese investors favor stock ETFs because they are less volatile than individual stocks or the broader market. With the index repeatedly hitting fresh highs, future challenges become more complex: sector rotation is rapid and single‑stock volatility is high, so the index is expected to trade in a high‑range consolidation. They recommend high‑dividend ETFs to add resilience to portfolios, especially those that combine semiconductor growth prospects. Such ETFs offer low volatility, steady income and potential capital gains from the AI boom, making them an optimal choice for current fund allocation.

ETF manager Hsieh Ming‑Chih of Qunyi Semiconductor Yield explains that Taiwan’s high‑dividend ETFs tend to feature high payouts together with growth potential, covering a broad range of industries to capture diverse sector dividends. Taiwan’s semiconductor revenue jumped 61% year‑over‑year in August, far above historical averages. In Q3, driven by AI‑related advanced processes and high‑end packaging, wafer‑foundry and packaging revenues are projected to grow 15‑20% quarter‑over‑quarter. Q4 is expected to benefit from seasonal momentum, with the sector likely posting double‑digit quarterly growth. As a key AI supply‑chain hub, Taiwan’s advanced fabs and packaging firms should continue to thrive, keeping the market poised for a traditional fourth‑quarter rally.
